images.title: Will the 70° piece fit?
images.purpose: Show six angles round a point, with one gap left, and a separate 70° wedge to test.
images.composition: A point in the left two thirds of the frame with seven rays; a loose wedge on the right.
exact_structure: A centre point with 7 dark rays round it, making 6 marked angles and one unmarked gap.
The 6 marked angles, going anticlockwise, labelled 40°, 60°, 50°, 30°, 40° and 90°, each shaded teal (#0072B2) with a small angle arc.
The remaining gap is left white with a reddish purple (#CC79A7) question mark inside it; it is a 50° gap.
On the right, a separate amber (#E69F00) wedge with its angle labelled 70°.
The angle sizes are drawn accurately, so the 70° wedge is visibly wider than the gap.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The gap is 360° − 310° = 50°, so the 70° piece does not fit.
